chapter_name: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
learning_objective: 🎯 Discover the mind-bending quantum reality where light behaves like physical particles (photons) and solid matter behaves like waves!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Light isn't a continuous wave; it's made of tiny, discrete energy packets called 'Photons'. The energy of a photon depends entirely on its frequency ($E = h\nu$), not its brightness.
When light of a sufficiently high frequency hits a metal surface, it knocks electrons completely out of the metal. If the frequency is too low, nothing happens, no matter how bright the light is!
The 'Work Function' is the minimum energy required to rip an electron from the metal. The 'Threshold Frequency' is the minimum frequency of light that contains exactly that much energy.
Energy is conserved! The energy of the incoming photon goes into freeing the electron (Work Function) and giving it speed. Equation: $K_{max} = h\nu - \Phi$.

If light can act like particles, can particles act like waves? Yes! De Broglie proposed that all moving matter has a wavelength associated with it: $\lambda = h/p$ (where $p$ is momentum). We just can't see the waves of large objects like cars.

fun_activity.title: ☀️ Solar Panel Magic
fun_activity.instructions: If you have a solar-powered calculator, cover the tiny solar panel with your finger. It stops working. The solar panel is utilizing the Photoelectric Effect to knock electrons loose and create a current to run the screen!

exam_tips: 📌 Stopping potential is independent of the intensity of incident light, but it directly depends on its frequency.
📌 Increasing the intensity of light only increases the number of emitted electrons (current), NOT their maximum kinetic energy.
📌 The Davisson-Germer experiment is the historical proof of the wave nature of electrons (electron diffraction).
quick_recap: ⭐ Light behaves as a wave while traveling (interference), but behaves as a particle when interacting with matter (photoelectric effect).
⭐ Photons have no rest mass, but they carry momentum!
⭐ Even you have a wavelength when you run, but it is unimaginably tiny because of your large mass.
